title: astra.registry.index/1
description: registry/v1/index.json — the catalogue the Astra client fetches. GENERATED from plugins/**; never hand-edited. Since 3.2 it is a SIGNED ENVELOPE: `signed` holds the catalogue and `signatures` holds Ed25519 signatures over SHA-256("astra.registry.index/1" ‖ 0x00 ‖ JCS(signed)), made with an index key that a root-signed trust.json delegates to. Nothing outside `signed` is authenticated — not `$comment`, not the `key_id` fields — and nothing outside it may be read as a fact. Two audiences share `signed`: the daemon's flat reader (id/name/version/description/platform_downloads) and everything from 2.9 on, which reads `releases[]` for the per-artifact sha256 and size. The flat fields are a projection of `releases[0]` from the same generator run, so they cannot disagree with it.

signatures.description: Empty in the committed tree: this repository holds no signing key, and CI signs the deploy candidate in the `publish` environment. An empty array says 'unsigned' out loud, where an absent member could not be told from a stripped one.

key_id.description: A HINT, for logs and key selection. The verifier tries every trusted key against every offered signature, so this string cannot make a signature verify and cannot stop one from verifying.

serial.description: Monotonic. Derived from the commit count of `main`, never read-and-incremented from a file — two merges landing at once would collide on that. The daemon refuses an index whose serial is lower than the highest it has already accepted (PRODUCTION_PLAN §3.2).

issued_at.description: When this catalogue was SIGNED, not when its content changed. Absent in the committed tree; bot/sign-index.mjs stamps it. A generator that stamped it would make a catalogue nobody edited for 31 days expire itself, and would make its own output unreproducible.

expires_at.description: issued_at + 30 days. Expiry downgrades Browse to a banner; it does NOT stop a cached, digest-pinned record from installing, because the digest is the security property and a digest does not expire. The hard block lives on revocations.json at 7 days (PRODUCTION_PLAN §5.5).

publishers.description: What the registry knows about the ACCOUNTS behind these listings, keyed by GitHub owner login. Present only for owners a listing points at. Inside `signed`, so the signature a client already verifies covers it — a badge is a claim the registry makes, and a claim outside the signature is one whoever serves the bytes could invent.

description.description: One line saying who this publisher is to Astra, for a person to read beside the badge. Optional; a client must render nothing when it is absent rather than inventing a default.

tier.description: A string rather than a closed client-side enum: a new tier should cost a registry edit and a locale key, not a proto change and an arm in every shell. A client MUST render on explicit membership — equal to `astra_team` or equal to `verified` — and never on the value merely being present, non-empty, or not-some-default. An unrecognised tier is not a badge.

last_confirmed_at.description: When the evidence last held. `verified` is stored as live evidence plus this date, not as a verdict, because a tier granted once and never revisited is a claim about who somebody used to be.

version.description: The latest listed release. Compatibility projection of releases[0].version.

description.description: The one-line card text. Projection of plugin.json's `summary`; named `description` because that is the field the daemon already deserialises.

readme.description: The plugin's own README, for the store's detail view. GitHub-flavoured markdown with NO RAW HTML and no image pointing anywhere but GitHub's asset hosts — both guaranteed by bot/lib/assets.mjs when this was derived, because by the time a client reads this the author is a stranger and the renderer is inside Astra's window. Inlined rather than linked so the bytes are covered by the index signature and so opening the store makes no request to a third party. Absent when the plugin ships no README. The 16384 here is a character bound and is the backstop, not the budget: what the registry enforces is 16384 UTF-8 BYTES, in bot/lib/assets.mjs (MAX_README_BYTES), which truncates to it, and in tools/build-index.mjs and tools/validate.mjs, which refuse over it. Bytes are never fewer than characters, so anything this schema accepts the byte cap has already had the final say on.

icon_url.description: The store card's picture. A `data:image/png;base64,…` or `data:image/svg+xml;base64,…` URI when the listing committed an icon (the normal case since bot/ingest.mjs started extracting one from the attested bundle), an `https://` URL for an older hand-written listing, and empty when there is neither. Deliberately unpatterned: a client renders whichever it is handed, and both forms have shipped.

downloads.description: Always 0. This registry counts nothing; see README §What is not here.

staging.description: true when the latest listed release has no artifact digest yet. Such an entry is deliberately absent from `platform_downloads` and `download_url`, so a client that only knows the flat fields cannot download it.

download_url.description: Legacy platform-agnostic URL. Empty except for a `noarch` release, which has genuinely one artifact for every host.

platform_downloads.description: Compatibility projection: platform key -> URL for the latest listed release. A `noarch` artifact is written under every supported platform key (PRODUCTION_PLAN §5.2), so no client needs to learn the word. Digest-free (staging) releases are omitted entirely.

releases.description: Newest first, by semver precedence. This is the authoritative half of the record.

publisher.description: The key into `signed.publishers`, i.e. the GitHub owner of `source.repo` — the only identity this registry proves. ABSENT when no reviewed record exists, and absence is the answer: a client that renders a badge from this field being present would badge every listing. Deliberately not the `author` string, which comes out of the plugin's own manifest and is whatever the author typed.

release.description: Copied through from the version file. `github_release` names a repo and a tag; `direct` names the `base_url` its artifacts sit under. schema/version-v1.json says why the second kind exists and where it is allowed.

url.description: Any https origin; which one is legal is decided by this release's `release` object and enforced in tools/validate.mjs, not by a pattern that can only describe GitHub.

sha256.description: sha256 of the whole .astraplugin file. Absent only on a staging entry, which is uninstallable by construction.
